subject: Fitting growth models in blavaan using the formula function

messages.author: 0ee8ae7c0d185529
messages.subject: Fitting growth models in blavaan using the formula function
parts:
Hi all,

I am interested in knowing if the formula function in R can be used with blavaan.  Specifically,  I have been successfully able to use the formula function in R to fit 4 simple Stan glm models

```
fits <- list()

fits[[1]] <- stan_glm(PV1READ ~ 1, data = PISAdata, seed = 832762) # This is the baseline model
fits[[2]] <- update(fits[[1]], formula = PV1READ ~ Female + ESCS + HOMEPOS + ICTRES) # model 1 variables
fits[[3]] <- update(fits[[1]], formula = PV1READ ~ JOYREAD + PISADIFF + SCREADDIFF + SCREADCOMP) # model 2 variables
fits[[4]] <- update(fits[[1]], formula = PV1READ ~ METASUM + GFOFAIL + MASTGOAL + SWBP + WORKMAST + ADAPTIVITY + COMPETE) # model 3 variables
fits[[5]] <- update(fits[[1]], formula = PV1READ ~ PERFEED + TEACHINT + BELONG) # model 3 variables
```
This is followed by further code for what I needed to do.  What I would like to do is use this formula and update functionality for fitting different growth models.  Is that possible?

Thanks

messages.author: 645e2b041ea2a63e
messages.subject: Re: Fitting growth models in blavaan using the formula function
parts:
Hi David,

There is not currently an update() method for blavaan. If you try to use it, I believe R will try to use update() from lavaan and throw some errors.

For rstanarm, I am not sure that update() gives you any computational speedups. I think it just saves typing because you only need to specify a new formula without sending in the data and other arguments. I think that an approach like the following would also work for blavaan:

modelargs <- list(formula = "PV1READ ~ 1", data = PISAdata, seed = 832762)
fits[[1]] <- do.call("stan_glm", modelargs)

modelargs$formula <- "PV1READ ~ Female + ESCS + HOMEPOS + ICTRES"
fits[[2]] <- do.call("stan_glm", modelargs)

modelargs$formula <- "PV1READ ~ JOYREAD + PISADIFF + SCREADDIFF + SCREADCOMP"
fits[[3]] <- do.call("stan_glm", modelargs)


and so on.

Ed
